items.definition: You say no when you do not want something, or when something is not true.
items.example: No, I don't want any more peas.
items.picture_idea: A child shaking their head with a hand held up.
items.definition_previous: A word you say to refuse something or to say that something is not true.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: Your nose is in the middle of your face. You smell things and breathe air with it.
items.picture_idea: A smiling child pointing to the nose on their face.
items.definition_previous: The part of your face that you use to smell and breathe.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the organ of smell and entrance to the respiratory tract; the prominent part of the face of man or other mammals

items.definition: Night is the dark part of the day, after the sun goes down. Many people sleep then.
items.example: The stars come out at night.
items.picture_idea: A dark sky with a moon and stars over a house.
items.definition_previous: The time when it is dark and people usually sleep.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the time after sunset and before sunrise while it is dark outside

items.definition: You say now to mean at this moment, not later. If you want something right away, you say now.
items.definition_previous: At this moment; not later.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: at the present moment

items.definition: Off means not on or not working. When you turn a light off, it goes dark.
items.explanation: We say the light is off when it is not shining.
items.picture_idea: A hand flipping a light switch down, with a dark lamp.
items.definition_previous: Not on; away from a place, or not working.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: no longer on or in contact or attached

items.definition: Use on to say something is sitting on top of something else, like a cup on a table.
items.example: The cup is on the table.
items.picture_idea: A cup sitting on top of a table.
items.definition_previous: Touching the top of something, or working.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: One is the number 1. If you have one ball, you have a single ball, not two.
items.picture_idea: A single red ball with the number 1.
items.definition_previous: The number 1; a single thing.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: To open a door or a box, you move it so it is not shut. Then you can look inside.
items.picture_idea: A child opening a door wide.
items.definition_previous: To move something so that it is not closed.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: cause to open or to become open

items.definition: You say ouch when something hurts you. If you bump your knee, you might say ouch.
items.picture_idea: A child holding a knee with a pained face.
items.definition_previous: A word you say when something hurts.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: Out means going from the inside of a place to the outside. You go out of the house to play.
items.picture_idea: A child walking out through a front door into a garden.
items.definition_previous: Not inside; going from inside to outside.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: moving or appearing to move away from a place, especially one that is enclosed or hidden

items.definition: A pig is a farm animal with a curly tail and a flat nose. It says oink and likes mud.
items.example: The pig is rolling in the mud.
items.picture_idea: A pink pig with a curly tail standing in mud.
items.definition_previous: A pink farm animal that says oink.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: domestic swine

items.definition: To play is to have fun with toys or games. You can play with blocks or a ball.
items.example: Can we play with the blocks?
items.picture_idea: Two children stacking colorful blocks.
items.definition_previous: To have fun with toys or games.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be at play; be engaged in playful activity; amuse oneself in a way characteristic of children

items.definition: You say please when you ask for something, to be polite. You say please when you want more juice.
items.picture_idea: A child holding out an empty cup and asking politely.
items.definition_previous: A polite word you use when you ask for something.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: A potty is a small seat shaped like a bowl that sits on the floor. You use it to go pee or poo.
items.example: I need to go on the potty.
items.picture_idea: A small child-sized potty on a bathroom floor.
items.definition_previous: A small toilet for a young child.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a receptacle for urination or defecation in the bedroom

items.definition: You pull a wagon or a door by holding it and moving it toward you.
items.example: Pull the wagon to the tree.
items.picture_idea: A child pulling a toy wagon by its handle.
items.definition_previous: To hold something and move it toward you.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: cause to move by pulling

items.definition: You push something by pressing on it so it moves away from you, like a swing or a door.
items.picture_idea: A parent pushing a child on a swing.
items.definition_previous: To press something to make it move away from you.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: move with force

items.definition: Use put when you take something and set it down in a spot, like a toy in a box.
items.example: Put the toy in the box.
items.picture_idea: A child placing a teddy bear into a toy box.
items.definition_previous: To place something somewhere.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: put into a certain place or abstract location

items.definition: Rain is water that falls from clouds in small drops. You get wet in the rain if you have no umbrella.
items.example: I can hear the rain on the window.
items.picture_idea: Gray clouds with raindrops falling on a window.
items.definition_previous: Water that falls from the clouds in drops.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: water falling in drops from vapor condensed in the atmosphere

items.definition: When you read, you look at words and know what they say. You can read a book or a sign.
items.explanation: The past form is spelled the same but sounds like "red".
items.picture_idea: An adult reading a picture book to a child on their lap.
items.definition_previous: To look at words or pictures in a book and say or understand them.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: interpret something that is written or printed

items.definition: Red is the color of ripe strawberries and fire trucks.
items.picture_idea: A bright red ball or a ripe strawberry.
items.definition_previous: The color of a strawberry or a fire truck.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: of a color at the end of the color spectrum (next to orange); resembling the color of blood or cherries or tomatoes or rubies

items.definition: To run is to move fast on your feet, faster than walking. Dogs and people run in the park.
items.example: The puppy likes to run in the park.
items.picture_idea: A child running across a grassy field.
items.definition_previous: To move fast on your feet.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: move fast by using one's feet, with one foot off the ground at any given time

items.definition: Sad is how you feel when something bad happens. You may cry if your balloon pops.
items.example: The little boy is sad because his balloon popped.
items.picture_idea: A child with a frown and a tear, holding a popped balloon.
items.definition_previous: Feeling unhappy.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: experiencing or showing sorrow or unhappiness

items.definition: Shoes cover your feet when you walk outside. You put them on before you go out.
items.explanation: This word is usually used in the plural. One of them is a shoe.
items.picture_idea: A pair of small sneakers side by side.
items.definition_previous: Things you wear on your feet when you go outside.

definition_basis.note: no WordNet meaning fit; written by Claude
definition_basis.batch_note: Headword is a plural form; the only WordNet meaning for 'shoes' is the idiom 'in someone's shoes', which does not fit. 'Shoe' would be the usual headword.

items.definition: You sit by resting your bottom on a chair or the floor. Sit down when you want to rest or eat.
items.picture_idea: A child sitting on a small chair.
items.definition_previous: To rest with your bottom on a chair or the floor.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be in a position in which one's upper body is largely upright and supported by one's backside

items.definition: When you sleep, your eyes are closed and your body rests, usually at night. You may dream.
items.example: The baby will sleep in her crib.
items.picture_idea: A baby sleeping in a crib with a blanket.
items.definition_previous: To rest with your eyes closed, like at night.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be asleep

items.definition: A snack is a small bit of food you eat between meals. Fruit or crackers can be a snack.
items.picture_idea: A small bowl of crackers and apple slices.
items.definition_previous: A small amount of food you eat between meals.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a light informal meal

items.definition: You feel sorry when you wish you had not done something bad. You say "sorry" after a mistake.
items.example: I'm sorry I knocked over your tower.
items.picture_idea: A child looking down, next to a fallen block tower.
items.definition_previous: Feeling bad about something you did, or a word you say after a mistake.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: feeling or expressing regret or sorrow or a sense of loss over something done or undone

items.definition: A spoon is a tool with a small bowl and a long handle. You use it to eat soup.
items.picture_idea: A baby spoon with a bit of food on it.
items.definition_previous: A tool with a small bowl on a handle that you use to eat soup or cereal.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a piece of cutlery with a shallow bowl-shaped container and a handle; used to stir or serve or take up food

items.definition: You say stop when you want someone to not move or not go on. Cars stop at a red light.
items.picture_idea: A red stop sign or a hand held up flat.
items.definition_previous: To not move or not do something anymore.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: come to a halt, stop moving

items.definition: The sun is the bright light in the sky in the day. It gives us light and makes us warm.
items.picture_idea: A bright yellow sun with rays in a blue sky.
items.definition_previous: The bright round star in the sky that gives us light and heat in the day.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: any star around which a planetary system revolves

items.definition: You say thanks when someone gives you something or helps you. It shows you are glad.
items.explanation: It is a short way of saying "thank you".
items.picture_idea: A child smiling and taking a cookie from an adult.
items.definition_previous: A word you say to show you are grateful.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You say that to point to something away from you. Use it for the one over there.
items.picture_idea: A child pointing to a toy on a high shelf.
items.definition_previous: A word for pointing to something that is not close to you.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You say this to point to something close to you. If you hold a book, you say "this book."
items.picture_idea: A child holding up a book.
items.definition_previous: A word for pointing to something that is close to you.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: A toy is something made to play with. A ball and a puzzle are toys.
items.example: She put her toy in the box.
items.picture_idea: A toy box with a teddy bear, car, and blocks.
items.definition_previous: A thing that children play with.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: an artifact designed to be played with

items.definition: A tree is a tall plant with a thick trunk, branches, and leaves. Birds often sit in trees.
items.example: The bird sits in the tree.
items.picture_idea: A big tree with green leaves and a brown trunk.
items.definition_previous: A tall plant with a thick brown trunk, branches, and leaves.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a tall perennial woody plant having a main trunk and branches forming a distinct elevated crown; includes both gymnosperms and angiosperms

items.definition: You say up when something goes to a higher place. You say "up" when you want to be lifted.
items.explanation: A baby may say "up" to ask to be picked up.
items.picture_idea: A baby reaching both arms up toward a parent.
items.definition_previous: Toward a higher place.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: spatially or metaphorically from a lower to a higher position

items.definition: You wait when you stay where you are until someone comes or something happens. People wait in line.
items.example: Wait for me at the door.
items.picture_idea: A child standing by a door with a hand up.
items.definition_previous: To stay in a place or not do something until later.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: stay in one place and anticipate or expect something

items.definition: When you walk, you move on your feet, one step at a time. You can walk to the park.
items.picture_idea: A parent and child walking hand in hand on a path.
items.definition_previous: To move on your feet at a slow, steady speed.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: use one's feet to advance; advance by steps

items.definition: You use want to say what you would like to have or do. Say "I want juice" to ask for it.
items.picture_idea: A child reaching toward a cup.
items.definition_previous: To wish for something.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: feel or have a desire for; want strongly

items.definition: Water is the clear liquid you drink. It comes out of a tap and falls as rain.
items.example: Can I have a drink of water?
items.picture_idea: A clear cup of water.
items.definition_previous: The clear liquid that we drink and wash with.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a liquid necessary for the life of most animals and plants

items.definition: You say we when you talk about yourself and other people together. When you all go out, you say "we go."
items.example: We are going to the park.
items.picture_idea: A parent and child holding hands.
items.definition_previous: A word for you and me, or me and other people.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You say what when you ask about a thing. If you see something new, you ask "What is it?"
items.picture_idea: A child pointing at a covered box with a puzzled face.
items.definition_previous: A word you use to ask about a thing.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You say where when you ask about a place. If you cannot find your shoe, you ask "Where is it?"
items.picture_idea: A child looking around with hands out, searching for a lost shoe.
items.definition_previous: A word you use to ask about a place.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You say who when you ask which person. If someone knocks, you ask "Who is it?"
items.picture_idea: A child looking toward a closed door with a question mark.
items.definition_previous: A word you use to ask which person.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: Something is yellow when it is the color of a banana or a lemon.
items.picture_idea: A yellow rubber duck and a banana.
items.definition_previous: The color of a banana or the sun.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: of the color intermediate between green and orange in the color spectrum; of something resembling the color of an egg yolk

items.definition: You say yes when you agree or want something. If someone asks "Do you want milk?" you can say yes.
items.picture_idea: A child nodding and smiling.
items.definition_previous: A word you say to agree or to answer "I do" or "it is."

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: You say you when you are talking to someone. It means the person who is listening to you.
items.picture_idea: A child pointing to a parent.
items.definition_previous: A word for the person you are talking to.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: Something is yucky when it tastes, smells, or looks so bad that you do not like it.
items.explanation: This is a casual word, often used by children.
items.picture_idea: A child wrinkling their nose at a muddy shoe.
items.definition_previous: Tasting, smelling, or looking bad.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: highly offensive; arousing aversion or disgust

items.definition: You say yum when food tastes or smells very good. It shows you like it.
items.picture_idea: A smiling child rubbing their tummy with a banana.
items.definition_previous: A word you say when food tastes good.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: A zoo is a place where wild animals live so people can come and look at them.
items.example: We saw a lion at the zoo.
items.picture_idea: A zoo entrance with a lion and an elephant behind a fence.
items.definition_previous: A place where people go to see wild animals.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the facility where wild animals are housed for exhibition
